# Coding 0.6.4

This release adds project and global prompt templates, richer skill invocations,
and a safer full-access permission mode. It also keeps the composer stable while
session settings change and tightens several Go SDK request contracts.

## Highlights

- Prompt templates can be discovered from `~/.or/prompts/*.md` and
  `<workspace>/.or/prompts/*.md`, with project templates overriding global
  templates of the same name. Templates support positional arguments, defaults,
  slices, localized descriptions, and localized argument hints.
- Prompt templates and skills now share the composer slash menu. Successful
  invocations are recorded as structured metadata, so conversation history can
  render compact references without misclassifying ordinary slash-prefixed text.
- A Prompt Templates settings page groups project and global resources, previews
  Markdown content, reports invalid templates, and can refresh discovery without
  restarting Coding.
- Full access is available as an explicit permission mode. Enabling it requires
  confirmation that explains file, command, and network access before the session
  policy changes.

## Composer and settings

- Model, permission, and project controls are locked while a response is running,
  preventing an in-flight request from changing configuration unexpectedly.
- Updating model or permission settings no longer replaces or disables the whole
  composer. The editor remains stable while configuration controls and sending
  are temporarily locked until the update is confirmed.
- Settings updates are tracked per session, so a change in one side of a split
  workspace no longer blocks the other composer.
- Composer menus, model settings, permission controls, and the dark canvas have
  been refined for clearer hierarchy and more compact layouts.

## Go SDK compatibility and fixes

- The public model input constants are now `llm.ModelInputText` and
  `llm.ModelInputImage`, replacing `llm.Text` and `llm.Image`. Applications using
  the old names must update before compiling against v0.6.4.
- Explicit JSON `null` tool arguments are preserved. Nullable schemas can accept
  them, while non-nullable schemas now report a type mismatch instead of silently
  coercing null to a primitive zero value.
- Provider and request headers are merged case-insensitively using canonical HTTP
  names, with later request layers taking precedence consistently.
- Anthropic API key discovery no longer accepts the unsupported
  `ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN`; use `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

## Downloads and current limitations

DMG and ZIP builds are available for Apple Silicon (`arm64`) and Intel (`x64`)
Macs running macOS 12 or later. Windows and Linux builds are not included.

The macOS builds are ad-hoc signed, but are not signed with an Apple Developer
ID certificate and are not notarized. macOS may require approval under
**System Settings > Privacy & Security** after the first launch attempt.

The embedded browser should currently be used only with content you trust.
Dedicated isolation for untrusted pages is not complete.
